research_updates.title: Project boundary and operator chronology fixed before measurement
research_updates.notes: Direct discovery and gap closure searched Rocket/Quicken and Bedrock current pages, archived releases, Rocket history, SEC exhibits and exact web/archive terms for Quicken Loans Technology Center, Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, 1401 Rosa Parks, 1401 Rosa Parks Blvd. LLC, Ward 08 Items 8268-70 and 8286-9, and parcel 08008283-303 across 2013-2026. Material records opened were the May 20, 2014 construction release, June 30, 2015 opening release, January 19, 2015 SEC-filed lease and current Bedrock property page. The boundary is Quicken/Rocket's partial tenancy and data-center function inside a landlord-controlled mixed-use building: construction began May 20, 2014, the lease commenced January 19, 2015, and the grand opening occurred June 30, 2015. The current Bedrock 85,000-RSF figure conflicts with the opening, lease and assessor definitions, so it is not added or used to rescale evidence. Company-wide IT-team figures and other tenants remain outside scope.

source.title: Construction Underway On New, Detroit-based Quicken Loans Technology Center
source.notes: The operator says Quicken Loans and Bedrock began construction on May 20, 2014 at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard. It describes a 66,000-square-foot office and data-center complex with two 10,000-square-foot server rooms, half occupied by Quicken's technology team and an equal 33,000-square-foot portion available to another tenant. Its 1.4 MW statement was prospective and its 1,100-member IT-team figure was company-wide, so neither is treated here as a contemporaneous operating observation or site employment.

research_updates.title: Parcel, personal-property, bill, payment and exemption gap closure
research_updates.notes: The authoritative Detroit service resolves taxable commercial-improved parcel 08008283-303 and traces its November 6, 2017 combination to four predecessors: 08008268-70 at 1415 Rosa Parks, 08008283-5 at 1404 Vermont, 08008286-9 at 1430 Vermont and 08008290-303 at 1458 Vermont. Wayne County's live address search independently returns those real accounts and separately exposes personal-property accounts for Rocket Mortgage LLC (08990518.03), Rocket Close LLC (08990518.04), Rock Limited Partnership (08990518.05), and other occupants. The personal accounts cannot be collapsed into the landlord's real parcel or allocated to the data-center function. The city service's September 7, 2026 current/prior assessed values ($3,871,600/$3,781,000) and taxable values ($2,978,823/$2,900,510) conflict with the deprecated service values already carried in base evidence, so this append-only project fragment records the correction trail without creating duplicate same-period claims. The Wayne records inspected reported no outstanding delinquent taxes but exposed no current bill or payment amount. Michigan Treasury PA 198 and exact exemption searches produced no target certificate. Bills, payments, assessed personal property and project-specific exemptions therefore remain unknown rather than zero.

research_updates.title: Planning and permit audit preserves one bounded utility projection
research_updates.notes: Permit and land-use searches covered Detroit BSEED's live Accela/eLAPS search, Building, Trades and Certificate of Occupancy ArcGIS services, historical Detroit open-data references, City Council proceedings and City Planning Commission materials. The occupancy service returned no target record for the current or four predecessor parcel IDs, address range, Quicken, or Technology Center. Those bounded current-system non-results cannot establish original permit absence. BLD2019-03107 at 1415 is excluded as separate later interior work; ELE2019-03832 is later and valueless. The 2014 council resolution verifies alley/easement action and the $24,044.58 DTE estimate borne by the petitioner, while unpriced DWSD work remains a gap. The 2026 CPC presentation says Detroit zoning does not specifically address data centers; it is not the project's approval.

research_updates.title: Utility, resource and public-infrastructure searches stop at capacity
research_updates.notes: Sources checked for 2013-2026 were Detroit right-of-way permits, DTE Energy and Michigan Public Service Commission dockets/tariffs, Detroit Water and Sewerage Department rates and records, council utility clearances, operator and contractor facility descriptions, and exact address/entity searches for electric, gas, water, wastewater, reclaimed water, transmission, substation, tariff, meter, peak, bill, fiber and generator. Later no-fee permits ENG-21-19 and ENG-26-202 concern 123Net and Comcast work and are not assigned to original project cost or benefit. No facility meter, annual kWh, peak demand, electricity bill, gas use, total water, wastewater, reclaimed-water use, generator runtime, tariff arrangement, transmission/substation allocation or realized public-infrastructure cost was found. The cooling-design claim cannot establish zero total water.

research_updates.title: Workforce search adds an electrician subset, not total labor

research_updates.title: Candidate-by-candidate modeling review retains two bounded sensitivities
research_updates.notes: Every residual candidate was re-evaluated after third-pass gap closure. Resources: retain a low-confidence whole-facility annual electricity-throughput sensitivity of 3.066-12.264 million kWh using 25%, 50% and 100% of the reported 1.4 MW available-power nameplate; the high endpoint is a mathematical ceiling, not a prediction, and no PUE, cost or emissions factor is applied. Construction: retain a low-confidence electrician-only wage-payroll sensitivity of $682,344-$2,729,376 using about 70 electricians, the 234-day groundbreaking-to-report interval, a 40-hour week, BLS's $29.16 near-period area mean wage, and 25%, 50% and 100% duration shares. It excludes other trades, benefits, overtime and residence effects. Investment: reject; the MCE $4.8 million label, predevelopment property sale and $24,044.58 utility estimate have incompatible scopes and no final capital ledger. Suppliers: reject; named firms lack payments and locality. Operations/minimum coverage: reject; no source requires even one continuously staffed on-site position. Fiscal/public costs: reject; separate real and personal accounts still lack same-scope bills, payments, recipient revenue, project incentive value and marginal service cost. Community: reject; no project-specific recipient amount exists. County effects: reject; Wayne County aggregates lack facility linkage and a credible counterfactual. No lease-share allocation, PUE transfer, electricity-price or emissions extension, supplier multiplier, fiscal break-even, operating staffing model, community proxy or county causal claim is retained.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. project_description: The Quicken Loans Technology Center, now marketed as the Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, is a mixed office and data-center building at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard in Detroit's Corktown neighborhood. Quicken Loans and Bedrock began construction in May 2014, Quicken's lease commenced January 19, 2015, and the company held the grand opening on June 30, 2015. The opening materials describe a 66,000-square-foot complex with two 10,000-square-foot server rooms, while Quicken's lease covers 35,920 rentable square feet; this account therefore separates Quicken/Rocket's partial tenancy and data-center function from the landlord's larger property, combined parcel, later work, and other tenants.
